questions.q: Why save the whole scikit-learn Pipeline with joblib instead of only the fitted LogisticRegression?
options: Pipelines train faster than classifiers
joblib cannot save a bare classifier
It makes the file smaller
The imputing, scaling, and encoding learned in training must be applied identically at scoring time, so they travel with the model
questions.explain: Scoring raw feature rows requires the same medians, scaling, and encoding fitted in training. Saving the pipeline keeps them together and prevents training-serving skew.

questions.q: Why does the model card record library versions such as scikit-learn 1.1.2?
options: It is required by the joblib file format
So the model loads and behaves identically, since a joblib file should be loaded with the same scikit-learn version that saved it
To display in the API response
Because Docker refuses to build without them
questions.explain: Pickled scikit-learn objects can break or change behavior across versions. Recording and pinning versions lets you rebuild the same environment.

questions.q: Why is the 10% capacity limit applied in the batch job rather than in the single-customer API?
options: APIs cannot use probabilities
Batch jobs are always more accurate
The capacity limit is a rank within a whole list, which a single-customer request cannot know
Because the model outputs ranks, not probabilities
questions.explain: 'Top 10%' only exists relative to other customers scored in the same run. The API returns a probability and whether it clears the break-even; the batch job ranks the list.

questions.q: An API request arrives with plan = "Platinum", which the model never saw. The contract returns a 422 error. Why is that a deliberate design choice?
options: An unknown category is an upstream data problem worth surfacing, rather than something to score silently and possibly wrongly
422 is the code for a successful request
Pydantic cannot handle strings
The model would crash on any unseen category
questions.explain: The pipeline could technically encode it as all zeros, but silently scoring inputs outside the contract hides data problems. Failing loudly makes them visible.

questions.q: The Dockerfile in this lesson was shown but not run. Why does the lesson say so explicitly?
options: Dockerfiles cannot be tested
Docker is not used in machine learning
Docker was not available on the machine, and claiming a tested container would be false; honesty about what was verified matters
The Dockerfile is only for decoration
questions.explain: Everything else in the lesson was executed and its output shown. The container recipe was not, so it is labeled 'not run here' rather than presented as verified.
